summary: The first real Aureline operator action-plan / checklist workspaces — incident response, support remediation, and admin access review — as ordered, ownership-bearing next-step plans over canonical incident/support/admin objects. Each item keeps its local check-off distinct from any external mutation, links canonical evidence, carries approval/policy state and due/expiry, and never lets a local checkoff resolve a provider-owned object; plans declare explicit scope and boundary truth before share/export and freeze a snapshot handoff that preserves every truth field, all bound to the operator-surface matrix.

plans.label: Incident response plan
plans.summary: The ordered response plan for the auth-latency incident: observe and verify, apply the confirmed managed config change, escalate to the provider and stage a rollback on the separate execute-and-confirm path, and communicate. A checked-off step never implies the provider ticket or deployment changed.
plans.boundary_note: A mutating step discloses its approval admission and external-mutation state, and never implies a managed apply happened just because the box is checked.

export_gate.crosses_on_share: Item titles, intents, ordered local check-off states, external-mutation states, approvals, evidence refs, due/expiry, and ownership become visible to the workspace; raw provider payloads, credentials, and endpoint URLs never cross.

items.time_reason: Overdue: rollback readiness was due 30m ago and is still pending approval.

items.intent: Share current state and next checkpoint with stakeholders.

invariants.statement: Every plan binds the action-plan matrix surface family by the matrix's own surface id.
Every plan addresses a canonical aureline:// subject, and every item's external object and linked evidence are canonical handles.
Every plan's items form a contiguous 1..n order.
Every item names a written intent, an owner, and a decision right.
The set proves all six item classes — observe, verify, mitigate, rollback, communicate, and custom — without collapsing them.
An item resolves its external object only when its mutation is executed and confirmed, never from a local check-off; at least one locally-done item leaves its external object unresolved.
An externally linked item names a canonical object, a real mutation state, and a mutation note; a local-only item carries none of these.
Every item preserves its approval state with a reason when non-authorized, and a confirmed mutation held approval authority.
Every linked evidence ref is a canonical handle, and every verification step links at least one.
Every item's deadline state agrees with its due/expiry timestamps, and overdue/expired items carry a reason.
Every skipped or locally-blocked item carries a written local note.
Every plan declares a scope and a matching export gate that names what crosses the boundary on share/export and requires acknowledgement above private scope.
The set proves a private, a workspace-shared, and an org-shared plan.
Each plan's frozen handoff equals re-exporting it and is labeled snapshot_only.
Each handoff preserves the exact ordered items, the computed progress, and the boundary-truth sentence.
Progress reports local check-offs and confirmed external resolutions as separate counts, and at least one plan has more local check-offs than resolved external objects.
Every plan offers a local-safe local check-off and a separate preview-mutation action, and each action's local-safe flag is computed.
The incident-response, support-remediation, and admin-access-review plans are all present.
Plan ids and item ids are unique.
